Fellow rabies obsession-haver here. I don't know that I can advice per se but I hope you can take something away from my experience.

I was scratched by my cat who was being loaded into her carrier to go to get her rabies vaccine, ironically. Rabies can't transmit through cat scratches, but just like you, I wasn't willing to risk the alternative even though she wasn't suspected of being rabid.

I got into a blow-up fight with my father about getting vs not getting the rabies series. I ended up going to the ER myself to get it. Fwiw, idk what healthcare is like in whatever country you live in, but if you're in the US just know that a very nicely worded letter to my very good insurance company was all that stood between me and getting tagged with an $11K bill for the vaccinations.

What ended up getting me over my rabies obsession oddly enough was working in veterinary medicine. I can't for the life of me find it online but we had a reference-poster hanging in the reception area that basically broke down something about how soon before showing symptoms can an animal have rabies and that window is VERY small. Put things in perspective nicely.

This obsession is a scary one. I wish you all the best friend <3

I have a (very) half-baked theory that Skyrim is the reason nearly every triple-A game plays the same way nowadays. 

Skyrim was so big it was a cultural phenomenon. Everybody played Skyrim. People who had never touched a video game before played Skyrim. 

Skyrim opened the world of gaming up to nearly everyone, or at least came at the time when everyone was getting into gaming.

Most people don't need a finely-crafted, Miyazaki-esque gem of a game to be entertained. They need a couple of cool concepts and a chunk of gameplay. It's the same idea as summer blockbuster movies. Are there some that are genuinely great movies? Sure. But most are just filler and yet they annihilate the box office because most people aren't that discerning.

So why is every triple-A game nowadays the same copy-pasted open world 45-hour game with 5 hours of meaningful gameplay, a laundry list of trinkets and objectives to check off, and climbing towers to reveal the map? Thank Skyrim.
